cc_admin_intro: Configure the cookie consent banner shown to visitors. All strings can be translated via the plugin's lang/ files. The visitor's choice is stored in localStorage, no server-side cookie is required.
cc_status_on: Enabled — visitors are asked for consent
cc_status_off: Disabled — no banner is shown, no consent is asked (may be non-compliant if you have EU visitors)
cc_enabled_label: Enable the cookie consent banner on the front-end
cc_expiration_hint: After this delay the banner reappears so the visitor is re-prompted. 180 days (6 months) is the CNIL's recommended maximum.
cc_show_reject_label: Show a "Reject all" button next to "Accept all" (recommended for GDPR compliance)
cc_appearance_hint: Colors used by the banner and settings modal on the front-end. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in palette.
cc_categories_hint: Which cookie categories the visitor can opt into. "Strictly necessary" is always on and cannot be disabled. Uncheck a category if your site never uses it, so the visitor is not shown an irrelevant toggle.
cc_cat_analytics_admin_desc: Enable if your site uses analytics tools like Plausible, Umami, Matomo, or Google Analytics.
cc_cat_marketing_admin_desc: Enable if your site uses ad tracking, retargeting pixels, or conversion tracking (Google Ads, Meta Pixel).
cc_privacy_hint: Optional. Displayed inside the banner as a "Privacy policy" link. Accepts either a full https:// URL or a site path starting with / (e.g. /privacy/). Leave empty to hide the link.
cc_shortcode_intro: GDPR requires visitors to be able to change or withdraw their consent at any time. Paste this shortcode anywhere — in the site footer text, a menu item, your privacy policy page — and it will render as a text link that opens the preferences modal when clicked. No floating button, no imposed UI.
cc_shortcode_note: The link text can be customized in the plugin's lang/ files (key: cc_settings_link_label). Default is "Cookie settings".
